correctness.rationale: For a binary valuation with both colors cofinal, Box is constant on the four-element Boolean algebra generated by p, so all modal depths have four truth sets. Otherwise finite alternating color runs give a surjective bounded morphism to the finite reflexive chain C_r, with exact preservation of modal truth. A depth-d state type consists of its color and set of accessible depth-(d−1) types; characteristic formulas define every realized type. Induction shows q_d=min(r,d+2): at depth d the last d states are individually distinguished, while the unresolved prefix remains grouped by color, and one further suffix state splits per step. The resulting Boolean algebra has 2^{q_d} elements and stabilizes sharply at max(0,r−2). Edge cases r=1,2, d=0 and both colors cofinal are consistent with the formulas. Independent exhaustive finite checks corroborate but do not prove the infinite assertion.
residual_risks: Finite exhaustive checks cover only chains through length 11 for type equivalence; infinite model follows by the explicit bounded-morphism argument, not extrapolation.
No claims about strict forward relation, multi-atom valuations, arbitrary transitive orders or computational efficiency of finding the runs.

Shapirovsky and Agnew prove broader qualitative local finiteness, not a valuation-parametric optimal atomic partition or depth-growth formula. value.rationale: The canonical reflexive natural-number frame has qualitatively locally finite complex algebra but its single-generator sizes and depth filtration need not be uniformly bounded. The all-valuations theorem identifies exact atoms by color runs or cofinality, determines every size 2^r, and gives sharp unbounded stabilization depth max(0,r−2). This is a complete natural structural classification of a concrete invariant, not arbitrary data sampling; one can use it as an exact benchmark for bounded modal equivalence, tuned partitions and expressivity versus modal depth. It does not claim a general frame theorem or paper-sized contribution.
residual_risks: The classification uses elementary combinatorial ingredients, so significance is in the exact natural boundary and sharp depth, not a new generic modal technique.
The invariant is restricted to one Boolean generator and reflexive omega; extension to richer valuations is unaddressed.

final_claim: For the reflexive Kripke frame (N,<=), one Boolean proposition p with arbitrary valuation X, and the truth-set Boolean algebras B_d(X) generated by finite modal formulas of box-depth<=d: if X and N\X both are infinite, |B_d|=|B|=4 for all d>=0. Otherwise X is eventually constant with r>=1 alternating maximal monochromatic runs (last run infinite), and |B_d|=2^{min(r,d+2)} for all integer d>=0, |B|=2^r, its atoms are the r runs, and least stabilization depth is max(0,r-2). Hence every power 2^r occurs and stabilization depth is unbounded.
limitations: This is an exact one-generator theorem for reflexive (N,<=), not arbitrary finite/transitive frames nor strict future or additional atoms.
Finite checks are bounded consistency tests, not infinite-model proofs. The analytical quotient and induction carry the infinite assertion.
Potential equivalent old calculation under unary temporal types or one-generated modal algebras remains a genuine priority uncertainty.
